instructions:
# Slides

Slides is a slide deck editor and presenter. Each document in the `decks` collection is one presentation. Decks you save appear in the user's Slides app (https://slides.freeappstore.online) the next time it is open and signed in, on every device. The user can then edit, present and export them.

## Making a good deck

- Ask what the talk is for, who the audience is and how long it is, unless that's already clear. Plan roughly one slide per 1–2 minutes: 6–12 slides for a short talk, rarely more than 20.
- Start with a `title` slide and end with a closing slide (summary, call to action or "Thank you" with contact details).
- Use `section` slides to divide longer decks into parts.
- One idea per slide. Keep a slide to 3–6 bullets of a few words each; put the detail in `notes`, which only the presenter sees.
- Vary the layouts: a `stat` for a key number, a `quote` for a voice, `two-column` for comparisons or before/after.
- Write real content for the topic. Don't use lorem ipsum.

## Document shape

```json
{
  "title": "Deck title",
  "theme": "midnight",
  "font": "display",
  "slides": [
    { "layout": "title", "title": "Deck title", "body": "Subtitle · Name · Date" },
    { "layout": "content", "title": "Why now", "body": "- First point\n- Second point\n  - A nested point", "notes": "What to say here." }
  ]
}
```

Only `title` and `slides` (each with `layout` and `title`) are required; the app fills in everything else. Don't send `id`, `createdAt` or `updatedAt`: the app and server manage them. When updating a deck, send the whole `slides` array: saving replaces top-level fields as a whole.

## Layouts and their fields

| layout | `title` | `body` | `body2` | `image` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | deck title, large and centred | subtitle | – | – |
| `content` | slide heading | bullets or paragraphs | – | – |
| `two-column` | slide heading | left column | right column | – |
| `image` | slide heading | caption | – | image URL |
| `section` | section name, very large | short subtitle | – | – |
| `quote` | optional small heading | the quote (no quote marks) | who said it | – |
| `stat` | the number itself, e.g. `"87%"`, `"$4.2B"`, `"3×"` | what the number means | – | – |
| `image-text` | slide heading | text beside the image | – | image URL |

### Text in `body` and `body2`

- A line starting with `- ` is a bullet; indent two spaces per level to nest (up to 3 levels).
- Blank lines separate paragraphs. Use `\n` for line breaks inside the JSON string.
- Inline `**bold**`, `*italic*` and `` `code` ``; fenced code blocks with ``` work too.

### Images

Use `https://` URLs of images that are publicly reachable and that you are allowed to use. Never embed `data:` URLs: a deck document must stay under 64 KB.

### Speaker notes

`notes` on any slide: plain text the presenter sees in the presenter view, never shown on the slide.

### Text style (optional)

On `content`, `two-column`, `section` and `image-text` slides:
- `align`: `"left"` (default) or `"center"`.
- `size`: `"small"`, `"medium"` (default) or `"large"` for the body text. Use `"large"` for slides with only a few words.

## Themes (`theme`)

Light/dark-adaptive (follow the app's light or dark mode): `paper` (default, clean white), `contrast`, `bold` (blue), `soft` (pale blue), `sky`, `mint`.
Always dark: `midnight` (navy and gold), `graphite` (charcoal and teal), `forest` (deep green and cream), `plum` (purple and pink), `terminal` (black and green, good with the `mono` font).
Strong colour: `sunset` (orange–pink–purple gradient), `ocean` (blue–teal gradient), `lemon` (yellow and black).

## Fonts (`font`)

`classic` (default: serif headings, sans body), `sans`, `serif`, `mono`, `display` (bold uppercase headings), `system` (the device's own font).

Pick a theme and font that fit the audience: e.g. `paper` + `sans` for business updates, `midnight` + `display` for pitches, `sky` + `system` for lessons, `graphite` + `serif` for portfolios.

decks.description: One document per presentation: a title, a theme, a font and an ordered list of slides. Private to the signed-in user.

id.description: Managed by the app; omit when creating slides.

title.description: Heading; the number on a stat slide.

body.description: Main text. Lines starting with '- ' are bullets.

image.description: https:// image URL for image and image-text slides.

notes.description: Speaker notes, never shown on the slide.
